newsitem.title: UK: Italy's Ciampi calls for EBRD help in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi calls for EBRD help in Albania.

text.p: Italian foreign minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi on Monday called for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to play its part in helping strife-torn Albania.

"The current crisis in Albania requires new efforts from international financial organisations," Ciampi told the EBRD's annual conference in London. "I am confident the EBRD is ready to play its part as soon as the situation in Albania permits."
Italy's coalition government almost disintegrated last week after Prime Minister Romano Prodi proposed sending Italian troops into Albania.
Prodi survived a parliamentary vote by the skin of his teeth but at the cost of losing the support of his hard-left allies.
Ciampi said a closely coordinated international effort, involving the EBRD, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank would help stabilise the situation in Albania.
Prodi, visiting Albania, said 6,000 troops in a United Nations-backed force led by Italy would be deployed on Tuesday. That could prompt "the rebirth of Albania," he said.

The tiny, former communist country was plunged into chaos after millions of people lost life savings in "pyramid" savings schemes. The government has lost control of large parts of the country, particularly in the south.

"Albania is a tragic illustration of how hard-won progress in transition can be lost with frightening speed," EBRD President Jacques de Larosiere said. He promised to resume EBRD operations in the country once order had been restored.
